---
title: "_external-llox_from_llox_signal"
---

```{r}
cat(switch(
  to_report$params$llox_method,
  "pt_signal_mean" = paste(
    "LOD and LLOQ were defined as the lowest concentrations at which the mean signal exceeded 3×",
    "or 10× the mean signal of the blank (zero concentration point) respectively.",
    "DF (Detection Frequency) is defined as the percentage of samples where the signal exceeds 3×", 
    "the mean signal of the blank (zero concentration point)."
  ),
  "pt_signal_mean_plus_sd" = paste(
    "LOD and LLOQ were defined as the lowest concentrations at which the mean signal exceeded the",
    "mean signal of the blank (zero concentration point) plus 3× or 10× its standard deviation,",
    "respectively.",
    "DF (Detection Frequency) is defined as the percentage of samples where the signal exceeds", 
    "the mean signal of the blank (zero concentration point) by at least 3 standard deviations."
  )
))
if (to_report$params$use_rsd20) {
  cat(" Additionally, LLOQ required a signal RSD ≤ 20%.")
}
```

In order to fit a calibration curve to a meaningful range of concentration, the fitting range is adjusted.
The lower-limit of the range is chosen as the LLOQ.
Concentration points below the limit are excluded from the calibration curve.

As quite a few concentration points in the calibration curve samples of a chemical can be too far from the range observed in the samples for quantification (non-`CalCurve` and non-`QC` sample categories), the upper-limit of the calibration range is set. 
When there are sufficient number (≥ 3) of calibration points, that the points that produce signal after normalization exceeding the **highest** signal of the quantification samples are excluded except the lowest one.

If the lower-limit is set so high that fewer than three concentration points remain, that chemical is excluded from the calibration curve, because the curve cannot be fitted properly.
